3.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
3.text: "Thank you for being here on this glorious day, Mr. President and Mr. Vice President."

4.speaker: Narrator
4.text: The comically large amount of flags almost fully enveloped the buildings around the plaza in maroon, white and gold.

5.speaker: Narrator
5.text: At the entrance, Kesaro Kibener, the head of the National Front Party, was waiting for us in his iconic brown suit, watching the sky.

6.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
6.text: "As the former mayor of Jen, it is an honor to welcome you to this fine city."

8.speaker: Player
8.text: "It looks like you were a good mayor. Maybe you should think about running for local office again."

12.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
12.text: "Thanks for the kind words, but I'm sure I'll do an even better job as president. Besides, as you can see, our current mayor doesn't need my help."

13.speaker: Petr Vectern
13.text: "Thank you for organizing this, Mr. Kibener."

14.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
14.text: "The representatives of the PFJP and Minister Morgna are already inside the private meeting room. Hopefully we'll be finished before the festivities start."

15.speaker: Narrator
15.text: Kesaro gestured at the doors behind him.

19.speaker: Player
19.text: "Before we go in... Is everything ready within your party? You know the vote is approaching."

26.speaker: Player
26.text: "Before we go in... Is there a way to get you back on the table regarding the constitutional changes?"

27.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
27.text: "I am aware, Mr. President. Don't worry."

31.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
31.text: "The NFP will support the proposal if you hold up your end of your bargain."

32.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
32.text: "The NFP will support the proposal if you don't bring us new surprises at the last minute."

37.speaker: Player
37.text: "Before we go in... is there any way we can discuss how you can help us with the constitutional changes?"

38.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
38.text: "Besides, this is neither the time nor place to have such a conversation."

42.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
42.text: "Come now, Mr. President. There is no need for such talk."

44.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
44.text: "But let's just go inside now. Please follow me."

45.speaker: Narrator
45.text: We entered the building and walked through a massive conference hall until we approached a door towards the back of the building.

46.speaker: Narrator
46.text: Kesaro opened the doors for us and we entered the meeting room. PFJP leader Frens Ricter and his deputy Manoly Suheil was already seated at the left side of the table.

48.speaker: Narrator
48.text: As soon as we entered, Nia came to greet us. After showing our seats, Kesaro sat down next to his deputy, Remus Holstron.

49.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
49.text: "This is such a meaningful day. Thank you for coming here on behalf of your parties."

50.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
50.text: "But despite the festive atmosphere, we and the PFJP want to raise a few important concerns about the worrying state of affairs in Sordland."

51.speaker: Manoly Suheil
51.text: "I'm sorry to interrupt, but the analysis is about racism and radicalization in Sordland. And our main topic is the case of 'Ersen v. Sordland'. Please don't try to spin it."

52.speaker: Narrator
52.text: Kesaro stopped for a moment to check his notes.

53.speaker: Remus Holstron
53.text: "Mr. Ricter and his analysts have been working on an analysis of the Blud problem. As soon as they brought it up, we gave our support without reservations."

54.speaker: Petr Vectern
54.text: "Look at this guy. So full of himself."

55.speaker: Petr Vectern
55.text: "How did this clown convince the PFJP to have trilateral talks with them anyway?"

56.speaker: Player
56.text: "Honestly, it says more about Frens and the PFJP."

57.speaker: Player
57.text: "Probably the same reason why we're here. It's Victory Day, remember?"

58.speaker: Player
58.text: "He's a dangerously competent man, Petr. We should be cautious with him."

62.speaker: Player
62.text: "Try not to agitate him, Petr. Don't forget, he's our partner for now and we need his vote."

63.speaker: Petr Vectern
63.text: "How can I forget? Lucian nagged about the importance of the day for 20 minutes straight. It broke my soul."

67.speaker: Narrator
67.text: Seeing us arrive, Kesaro approached us with a smile.

69.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
69.text: "Of course, Ms. Suheil. Mr. Holstron just wanted to point out that this analysis was focused mainly on topics related to the Bludish people."

70.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
70.text: "I want to give the word to Mr. Ricter to explain the issue."

73.speaker: Frens Ricter
73.text: "Our analysis of the current tensions between the Bludish and Sordish population in Sordland displays a worrying picture."

74.speaker: Frens Ricter
74.text: "The increasingly discriminatory actions of the Governor of Bergia are resulting in the radicalization of many young Bludish people."

81.speaker: Player
81.text: "Why are we discussing this on Victory Day?"

82.speaker: Player
82.text: "I refuse to discuss this topic without any Bludish representation."

85.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
85.text: "Let's get back on track, ladies and gentlemen."

86.speaker: Frens Ricter
86.text: "Distressingly, it exploded out of control after the presidency gave support to Operation Bear Trap."

87.speaker: Frens Ricter
87.text: "Distressingly, the number of radicals have almost doubled after the implication of our armed forces in the Operation Bear Trap."

88.speaker: Frens Ricter
88.text: "Distressingly, the number of radicals have increased significantly after Wehlen's Operation Bear Trap."

89.speaker: Frens Ricter
89.text: "Unfortunately, the NFP's Religious Harmony Bill was also signed into law despite our protests. Which did nothing to ease the tensions."

90.speaker: Player
90.text: "I'm surprised that your parties have conducted a joint analysis."

91.speaker: Manoly Suheil
91.text: "We thank the NFP for assisting our research, of course. But this is by no means a joint analysis. Our parties have vastly different opinions."

95.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
95.text: "That bill targets the secessionist propaganda apparatus. I must point out that the recruitment numbers of the BFF have significantly reduced since the law's implementation."

96.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
96.text: "As the threat the BFF poses is a direct one, this issue requires direct actions that lead to direct results -- which seem to be proving successful as fact-checked by the Vice President."

97.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
97.text: "I must also point out that the recruitment numbers of the BFF have significantly increased within Nurist communities."

98.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
98.text: "The Religious Harmony Bill would have directly crippled this network they established within our sanctuaries. As the threat the BFF poses is a direct one, this issue requires direct actions that would bear direct results."

99.speaker: Frens Ricter
99.text: "As much as I hate to say it, the threat of the Bludish Freedom Front is getting real again. The situation with Rumburg and Wehlen is very concerning."

100.speaker: Player
100.text: "It's good to see that the new laws are working."

101.speaker: Player
101.text: "I'm regretting my decision to sign that bill."

103.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
103.text: "I'm disappointed by the lack of action taken by the USP administration."

104.speaker: Player
104.text: "Your bill would have unnecessarily raised the already high tensions."

105.speaker: Player
105.text: "And what do you suggest we do?"

106.speaker: Player
106.text: "I'm regretting my decision to veto that bill."

108.speaker: Manoly Suheil
108.text: "You did well by vetoing it, Mr. President."

109.speaker: Remus Holstron
109.text: "They are working, but it is not enough."

110.speaker: Manoly Suheil
110.text: "You should have controlled your party before they gave support to that bill in the Assembly."

114.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
114.text: "Our suggestion is to finally enforce the official language of our country as stated in the constitution."

115.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
115.text: "One of my suggestions to you was to finally enforce the official language of our country as stated in the constitution."

116.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
116.text: "Of course, you have already promised to support it, so we are already aligned on that matter."

117.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
117.text: "We are working on the Unified Language Act. It is directly aimed at the breeding grounds of the Bludish Freedom Front."

118.speaker: Nia Morgna
118.text: "You can't take away the Bludish people's right to be educated in their own language. This is insane."

119.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
119.text: "Please read the proposal carefully. It does not take away anyone's rights. It only gives the state a way to control the radicalization in these schools that teach Bludish nationalist propaganda."

120.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
120.text: "True. It does not ban Bludish language or Bludish education. It will instead make Sordish mandatory to learn for everyone living in this country. This will only decrease the tensions in the long term."

121.speaker: Frens Ricter
121.text: "That's a fair point. However, the wording of the bill is far too vague to work as intended. It gives the government too much power over educational institutes."

122.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
122.text: "I disagree. The language is quite clear and is in line with the Constitution. But we can still improve it, of course. It is true that it gives more control, but it is a necessary compromise."

123.speaker: Player
123.text: "As I've promised before, I'll sign the bill when it reaches me."

124.speaker: Narrator
124.text: Manoly looked furious. She opened her mouth to respond, then read the room and closed it again.

128.speaker: Player
128.text: "I'll sign the bill if it reaches me."

129.speaker: Player
129.text: "I'll have to read it in detail to decide if I can support it."

130.speaker: Player
130.text: "I don't see how this helps with the situation."

131.speaker: Remus Holstron
131.text: "The police have infiltrated 32 BFF training grounds in remote towns around Bergia that posed as middle schools. Despite all the evidence, similar schools keep popping up."

132.speaker: Remus Holstron
132.text: "And so-called activists are constantly blocking Governor Bron's attempts to stop these schools, claiming he is attacking their *right to language*."

133.speaker: Player
133.text: "Even if the Assembly supports it, I will surely be using my veto on it."

138.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
138.text: "Then you'll see what happens with your constitution."

142.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
142.text: "I wouldn't be so quick, if I were you."

143.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
143.text: "The NFP would surely expect a gesture before the *big* vote, after all."

145.speaker: Manoly Suheil
145.text: "The PFJP will not allow this bill to pass the Assembly."

146.speaker: Frens Ricter
146.text: "Let's not make statements that the party hasn't agreed on yet."

147.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
147.text: "If I were you, I wouldn't stand in the way of the majority, Mr. President."

148.speaker: Petr Vectern
148.text: "Hold up, guys. Let's hear them out first. We are representing the parties of the Assembly here."

149.speaker: Petr Vectern
149.text: "That seems to be correct. The reports show that the new laws definitely struck a blow to the BFF's religious wing and their recruitment."

150.speaker: Narrator
150.text: Petr frantically looked through his papers.

151.speaker: Petr Vectern
151.text: "That is correct. The reports show that 39 Nurist sanctuaries in Bergia are now classified as 'red threats' by the authorities. Many priests in the region are also suspected of having ties to the BFF."

152.speaker: Narrator
152.text: Petr frantically looked through his papers.

153.speaker: Frens Ricter
153.text: "If I may continue with our analysis..."

154.speaker: Frens Ricter
154.text: "The situation is also connected to Rumburg, as everybody already knows. In the case of a future incursion, BFF forces in Sordland could become an existential threat."

155.speaker: Frens Ricter
155.text: "As much I now support a strict response against the BFF, it must also be coupled with the expansion of rights for the Bludish people. This is the only way to fight against radicalization."

156.speaker: Remus Holstron
156.text: "That is BFF propaganda. What rights are we talking about here? What can a Sord in Sordland do that a Blud cannot?"

157.speaker: Remus Holstron
157.text: "You are using soft language as a cover-up for your willingness to negotiate with terrorists. You are a BFF apologist, Mr. Ricter!"

158.speaker: Petr Vectern
158.text: "Let's refrain from making comments about the internal affairs of the USP."

159.speaker: Player
159.text: "That's why we have to remove the authority of the governor."

160.speaker: Player
160.text: "With all due respect, I already received this information from Internal Affairs. Tell us something we don't know."

161.speaker: Player
161.text: "Maybe the NFP influences you more than you think, Mr. Ricter."

162.speaker: Narrator
162.text: He adjusted his tie and continued.

164.speaker: Frens Ricter
164.text: "Our analysis matches with what the Ministry of Interior shared with us. But despite this fact, we believe the ministry is hiding information from us, which is actively fuelling the tensions behind the scenes."

165.speaker: Petr Vectern
165.text: "Please don't raise your voice, Mr. Holstron."

166.speaker: Remus Holstron
166.text: "Is the USP that desperate for Mr. Ricter's support now?"

170.speaker: Remus Holstron
170.text: "I didn't know you were Mr. Ricter's lawyer, Mr. Vice President."

171.speaker: Narrator
171.text: Remus shouted the last sentence. Petr tapped on the table to get his attention.

172.speaker: Narrator
172.text: Manoly bellowed out a loud laugh.

173.speaker: Player
173.text: "From now on, nobody speaks until the speaker finishes their point."

175.speaker: Narrator
175.text: Everybody went silent and looked at me.

176.speaker: Narrator
176.text: Manoly bellowed out a loud laugh.

178.speaker: Narrator
178.text: The mood in the room had turned sour.

179.speaker: Manoly Suheil
179.text: "Mr. Vectern is the last person to sway the PFJP."

181.speaker: Player
181.text: "This is a mess. I thought we were here for a proper meeting."

182.speaker: Manoly Suheil
182.text: "Mr. Vectern is the last person that we'd rely on to defend us."

183.speaker: Player
183.text: "Your bill would have made everything worse."

187.speaker: Manoly Suheil
187.text: "Mr. President. Mr. Vice President. And Ms. Minister. As you already know, there is a major Supreme Court case at the moment."

188.speaker: Frens Ricter
188.text: "We require your support with a more pressing matter. This might have very significant consequences for our Bludish citizens and may serve as a dangerous trigger if we're not careful."

189.speaker: Narrator
189.text: Frens gestured at Manoly. She carefully placed several pieces of paper in front of her.

190.speaker: Manoly Suheil
190.text: "Ishval Ersen is suing the Governor of Bergia, Phelix Bron, for infringing upon the liberties of Bludish people and demands that the constitution be revised."

191.speaker: Manoly Suheil
191.text: "Because of the argument and the implications, Phelix Bron and, consequently, the very constitution of Sordland is under trial. The fact is, he needs to be punished and the Constitution must be reviewed."

192.speaker: Remus Holstron
192.text: "With all due respect, Mr. Kibener, this bill is not strong enough. The Bludish language should be completely banned. You know people like Ms. Suheil or Ms. Morgna will never even vote for your watered-down bill."

193.speaker: Nia Morgna
193.text: "I was actively involved in this case. Because of the implications with the constitution, there is no way the Supreme Court will agree with Ishval Ersen on all of the points."

194.speaker: Narrator
194.text: Nia raised her hand and spoke.

195.speaker: Frens Ricter
195.text: "Not if all three parties of the Assembly support Ersen together. We can put pressure on them. And we only need them to agree on a few of those points."

196.speaker: Player
196.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_Hub_Option1"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_Hub_Option2"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_Hub_Option3"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_Hub_Option1"] == false)

198.speaker: Narrator
198.text: Kesaro repositioned himself on his chair and continued.

199.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
199.text: "For peace and harmony in Sordland, yes. But perhaps we must clarify the details first."

200.speaker: Frens Ricter
200.text: "This never happened before, Mr. President. They surely cannot ignore us if all three parties are united and if we provide them with our analyses."

201.speaker: Frens Ricter
201.text: "What do you want to know, Mr. President?"

203.speaker: Frens Ricter
203.text: "We did invite the representatives of the Workers Party of Bludia to join us, but they refused."

204.speaker: Remus Holstron
204.text: "Another proof that they have a different agenda. If they were genuinely concerned for the plight of their people, they would have come today."

205.speaker: Remus Holstron
205.text: "But their people shouldn't worry. The Sordish patriots are here to defend them instead."

206.speaker: Player
206.text: "And why do you think it would influence the Court's decision?"

207.speaker: Player
207.text: "All parties? Is the NFP really willing to support Ersen, Mr. Kibener?"

210.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
210.text: "Because the case is now in the hands of the Supreme Court, this ruling will influence all future implementation of the law and the decision-making of the lower courts."

211.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
211.text: "I and the NFP are ready to push for de-escalation and aid our nation during this dangerous time."

212.speaker: Narrator
212.text: Remus was visibly annoyed but kept himself silent.

213.speaker: Player
213.text: "What is the most likely outcome of this case?"
213.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_Hub_Option1"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_Hub_Option2"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_Hub_Option3"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_Hub_Option2"] == false)

214.speaker: Frens Ricter
214.text: "Besides, if the NFP can see the necessity in de-escalation, I'm sure the Sollist judges can too."

217.speaker: Remus Holstron
217.text: "As if the PFJP has the influence to change the outcome..."

218.speaker: Player
218.text: "Don't worry. Our armed forces are capable of handling any threat."

224.speaker: Player
224.text: "I'll be honest with you. I'm not feeling very comfortable talking about Bludish rights with the NFP."

225.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
225.text: "I understand where this comes from, Mr. President. But please do not act like we are an anti-Blud party. Don't forget, we have members and supporters with Blud blood too."

227.speaker: Frens Ricter
227.text: "I can't believe I'm saying this, but it's not. We normally don't trust government data, but our own analysis came up mostly in line with the reports from the Ministry of the Interior and the Ministry of Defense."

229.speaker: Nia Morgna
229.text: "If they ignore all of the points and strike against Ersen, Governor Bron will be free to follow his discriminatory policies without any obstacles."

230.speaker: Nia Morgna
230.text: "And in a possible future case, the Court's interpretation of the Ersen case will be the basis of all future rulings, which opens the way of suspending the rights of non-Sords."

231.speaker: Nia Morgna
231.text: "The first and most likely option is that the Supreme Court completely ignores the arguments and rejects it in its entirety."

232.speaker: Frens Ricter
232.text: "I'm afraid Mr. Kibener is right about this. If the Court ignores this case now, this may turn into something... massive. Therefore we have to pressure the Court not to escalate the already high tensions."

233.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
233.text: "I'll be straight with you, Mr. President. If the Court rules against Ersen, this will most likely turn into a BFF campaign for a Bludish revolution. We ask everybody to recognize this."

234.speaker: Player
234.text: "What do you really think will happen if the Court ignores it?"

236.speaker: Frens Ricter
236.text: "I wouldn't say this for most other topics, but in the case of the threat of the BFF and radicalization, you should maybe listen to your cabinet."

237.speaker: Player
237.text: "So you just *believe* in Hawker and hope for the best? I thought you would have a better plan than this."

238.speaker: Remus Holstron
238.text: "In my opinion, that would be the preferred outcome. If enemies do truly live within our borders, I'd rather have them show their true faces earlier than later."

240.speaker: Narrator
240.text: Manoly glanced at Frens. Her eyes showed her agreement with me.

241.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
241.text: "This is exactly what those damn Rums want. They are readying for war and waiting to use the tensions inside Sordland against us."

242.speaker: Frens Ricter
242.text: "I hope the armed forces will not be necessary. For the sake of us all."

243.speaker: Nia Morgna
243.text: "It would effectively erase any progress that has been made regarding Bludish rights, and will embolden anti-Bludish proponents to follow their actions freely."

245.speaker: Player
245.text: "And how does that affect the administration?"

246.speaker: Player
246.text: "That would be disastrous for our Bludish citizens."

247.speaker: Player
247.text: "Bludish rights and the BFF have been major issues for many decades now. I don't see how this case makes either any worse than before."

248.speaker: Player
248.text: "And how do you think the Supreme Court will react if we do it your way?"
248.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_PFJP_1"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_PFJP_2"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_PFJP_3"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_PFJP_4"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_PFJP_2"] == true) == false)

249.speaker: Player
249.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_PFJP_1"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_PFJP_2"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_PFJP_3"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_PFJP_4"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_PFJP_3"] == true) == false)

250.speaker: Frens Ricter
250.text: "Anyway... Do you have other questions, Mr. President?"

251.speaker: Remus Holstron
251.text: "...so that they can cry about *injustice* and ask Sordland's enemies to come and *save* them. I personally do not agree with the 'Bluds are Sords' Sollist crap."

252.speaker: Petr Vectern
252.text: "You have a point. But I must point out that 'Contana' is the word for a geographic entity, unlike 'Sord'."

253.speaker: Remus Holstron
253.text: "The reality is the Bluds do not respect nor recognize the laws and authority of Sordland. They'd rather separate themselves from Sords and protest the very laws that protect them..."

255.speaker: Frens Ricter
255.text: "We normally do not trust government data, but our own analysis came up mostly in line with the reports from the Ministry of the Interior and the Ministry of Defense."

256.speaker: Narrator
256.text: The threat in his tone was obvious.

257.speaker: Player
257.text: "I see your point. But I still don't understand why the NFP suddenly had a change of heart."

258.speaker: Player
258.text: "Why are you even comparing Sordland with United Contana? Are you alright, Mr. Kibener?"

259.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
259.text: "My point is people like *the Malenyev* do not call themselves Kyovian over Contanan. Why is it that Bluds cannot do the same? Why does Sordland have to be divided?"

260.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
260.text: "I disagree. This case is important for the greater good of the Sordish nation, and that is what the Nationalist Front stands for."

261.speaker: Player
261.text: "Because Contana has nothing to do with this and Article 6 is inherently racist."

262.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
262.text: "All I'm asking is, if even in United Contana, *the Malenyev* doesn't call himself Kyovian before Contanan, why is it that Bluds cannot do the same? Why does Sordland have to be divided?"

266.speaker: Frens Ricter
266.text: "We agree to come together in support of Ishval Ersen, but we believe our statement should include the acknowledgement of the inherent racism within the Constitution."

267.speaker: Manoly Suheil
267.text: "We must use this opportunity to show the flaws in the Constitution. If the Court agrees that there is in fact conflict between the Articles, or recognize the discrimi-"

268.speaker: Frens Ricter
268.text: "I can't believe I'm saying this, but he is right."

269.speaker: Player
269.text: "I agree with Mr. Kibener. A United Sordland is what we need."

270.speaker: Nia Morgna
270.text: "I can't believe the words being thrown around at this meeting."

271.speaker: Player
271.text: "And what is the position of the PFJP?"

272.speaker: Frens Ricter
272.text: "I personally somewhat agree with Mr. Kibener on this. However, our position as the PFJP is that Article 6 does indeed discriminate against non-Sords."

273.speaker: Player
273.text: "Neither can I. I think it's time we wrap this up."

274.speaker: Petr Vectern
274.text: "Ladies and gentlemen. You've heard the president. Let's sum it up and arrive at the point quickly."

275.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
275.text: "And the Hawker Court is going to listen to that?"

276.speaker: Petr Vectern
276.text: "I'm not sure if it's worth the risk right before the vote for our reforms. But the decision is yours."

277.speaker: Player
277.text: "Tell me why we should pressure the Court to admit discrimination within the Constitution."
277.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_PFJP_1"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_PFJP_2"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_PFJP_3"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_PFJP_4"] == true) and (Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_NFP_1"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_NFP_2"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_NFP_3"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_NFP_4"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_PFJP"] == true) == false)

278.speaker: Manoly Suheil
278.text: "Because it is the right thing to do, Mr. President. Now is not the time for weak and superficial actions."

279.speaker: Frens Ricter
279.text: "We can show the people of Sordland the reality of the situation and create a precedent for a future constitutional amendment of these Articles."

280.speaker: Player
280.text: "And the NFP is willing to join in with that statement?"
280.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_PFJP_1"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_PFJP_2"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_PFJP_3"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_PFJP_4"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_PFJP_1"] == true) == false)

281.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
281.text: "Besides, we do not agree with your 'inherent racism' hogwash. You have to state that it is your party's opinion and does not reflect the NFP. We won't take part in that."

282.speaker: Player
282.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_PFJP_1"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_PFJP_2"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_PFJP_3"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_PFJP_4"] == true) and (Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_NFP_1"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_NFP_2"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_NFP_3"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_NFP_4"] == true) and (Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_Nothing"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_PFJP"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_NFP"] == true)

283.speaker: Player
283.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_NFP_3"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_NFP_1"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_NFP_2"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_NFP_3"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_NFP_4"] == true) == false)

284.speaker: Petr Vectern
284.text: "That would make the statement look weak and disorganized. If there's no consistent strategy, I don't think it would work."

285.speaker: Frens Ricter
285.text: "It can work for the time being, but I believe we can push for a more comprehensive outcome."

286.speaker: Manoly Suheil
286.text: "Exactly. Our current Constitution fails to recognize the Bludish people. It is time we abolish the inherent racism in it."

287.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
287.text: "Because it is the only way to decrease tensions. And the Supreme Court can't afford to look hypocritical, so they'll have to take the Sollist side."

288.speaker: Player
288.text: "And how do you think the Supreme Court will react if we do it your way?"
288.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_NFP_2"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_NFP_1"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_NFP_2"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_NFP_3"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_NFP_4"] == true) == false)

289.speaker: Manoly Suheil
289.text: "Exactly. Unfortunately, our current constitution fails to recognize them. It is time we abolish the inherent racism in it."

290.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
290.text: "I do not understand why someone would go against such a broad and inclusive law. I don't see the commies criticizing their Contanan identity, when in fact that country is filled with different ethnicities."

291.speaker: Manoly Suheil
291.text: "Exactly. Unfortunately, our current Constitution fails to recognize Bludish people. It is time we abolish the inherent racism in it."

292.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
292.text: "This is exactly what those damn Rums want. They are readying for war and waiting to use the tensions inside Sordland against us."

293.speaker: Remus Holstron
293.text: "I still think this is admitting defeat against Sollism... But Mr. Kibener is right. The Rumburg situation demands extraordinary measures."

296.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
296.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Reform_PFJP_Convinced"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Relations_Frens_Bribed"] == false  and  Variable["BaseGame.Relations_Frens_Promise_Taurus"] == false) == false

298.speaker: Frens Ricter
298.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Reform_Reform_PFJP_Convinced"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Relations_Frens_Bribed"] == false  and  Variable["BaseGame.Relations_Frens_Promise_Taurus"] == false) == false

300.speaker: Petr Vectern
300.text: "But the PFJP's stance would be too radical for our party. I think it might be better to keep our administration out of this."

301.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
301.text: "The citizens of Sordland are Sords. The constitution clearly defines that in Article 6. It encompasses everybody. This shouldn't be up for debate."

302.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
302.text: "Does *the Malenyev* call himself Kyovian before Contanan? Why is it that Bluds cannot do the same? Why can't the Sord patriots wish for unity?"

303.speaker: Frens Ricter
303.text: "But let's not spoil the mood. We are here to unite under another topic today."

304.speaker: Narrator
304.text: He gave me a questioning look.

305.speaker: Frens Ricter
305.text: "I'm sure you will do your absolute best to pass the amendments nonetheless."

306.speaker: Narrator
306.text: He gave me a questioning look.

308.speaker: Player
308.text: "Tell me why we should try to convince them to reiterate their position on Article 6."
308.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_PFJP_1"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_PFJP_2"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_PFJP_3"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_PFJP_4"] == true) and (Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_NFP_1"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_NFP_2"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_NFP_3"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_NFP_4"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_NFP"] == true) == false)

309.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
309.text: "No. We are willing to give our support for Ersen for the violation of his right to property. But if you are going to go that way, we have to make two separate statements."

310.speaker: Manoly Suheil
310.text: "We have to try. If they truly care for the people, they will agree to it. If not, people will see the reality of the Sollist state apparatus."

311.speaker: Petr Vectern
311.text: "I don't think this would work, Anton."

313.speaker: Petr Vectern
313.text: "Hawker won't be influenced. Plus, it could further antagonize them against our reforms. We will definitely lose votes."

314.speaker: Petr Vectern
314.text: "In my opinion, the PFJP has the most to gain from this. They would be seen as the leaders of this table, not us."

315.speaker: Player
315.text: "Is the PFJP willing to join in with that statement?"
315.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_NFP_1"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_NFP_2"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_NFP_3"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_NFP_4"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_NFP_1"] == true) == false)

316.speaker: Frens Ricter
316.text: "As much as I don't agree with it, we are willing to compromise and join in."

317.speaker: Player
317.text: "I don't want to release a unified statement with the opposition. We will not involve ourselves in this case."

318.speaker: Narrator
318.text: The representatives of both parties looked at me with disappointment.

319.speaker: Player
319.text: "The USP will join the statement. We will argue that Bludish people are considered Sords before the law, as Mr. Kibener suggested."

320.speaker: Player
320.text: "The USP will join the statement. We will argue that Articles 6 and 7 are inherently discriminatory and in conflict with the rights of people, as Mr. Ricter suggested."

321.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
321.text: "That's great to hear. We will get to work immediately after the celebrations."

325.speaker: Nia Morgna
325.text: "I also agree that Chief Justice Hawker won't have a sudden change of heart because of it. But we must put pressure on the Justices nonetheless."

326.speaker: Nia Morgna
326.text: "I think I have made my own position clear. In the end, it is your decision."

334.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
334.conditionsRaw: Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_PFJP_1"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_PFJP_2"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_PFJP_3"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_PFJP_4"] == true

335.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
335.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_PFJP_1"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_PFJP_2"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_PFJP_3"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_PFJP_4"] == true) == false

338.speaker: Player
338.text: "We will stay out of it. This isn't worth the risk."

339.speaker: Player
339.text: "The USP will join the statement with the NFP. We will argue that Bludish people are considered Sords before the law, as Mr. Kibener suggested."

340.speaker: Frens Ricter
340.text: "But if you are going to go this way, we will still need to make our separate statement as party policy."

341.speaker: Narrator
341.text: Manoly was shaking in her seat in fury but managed to keep herself silent.

342.speaker: Frens Ricter
342.text: "That's great to hear. We will get to work immediately after the celebrations."

350.speaker: Petr Vectern
350.text: "If you are going to add the amendment Nia's been working on, this is the stance we should take."

351.speaker: Petr Vectern
351.text: "This could help get the winds of change behind us."

355.speaker: Nia Morgna
355.text: "As I already said, supporting the PFJP to put pressure on the court and declare that our constitution is inherently discriminatory will only do good for our new amendments."

356.speaker: Nia Morgna
356.text: "This is what we believe in, so we should make it public."

357.speaker: Nia Morgna
357.text: "I agree with Mr. Ricter and Ms. Suheil. I personally think we should join them in their statement."

361.speaker: Nia Morgna
361.text: "As I already said, supporting the NFP should be out of the question."

362.speaker: Player
362.text: "I think I have enough information about the NFP's position. Let's hear the other side."
362.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_PFJP"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_NFP_1"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_NFP_2"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_NFP_3"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_NFP_4"] == true) == false)

365.speaker: Player
365.text: "What do you suggest we do, Ms. Morgna?"
365.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_NFP_4"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_NFP_1"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_NFP_2"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_NFP_3"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_NFP_4"] == true) == false)

366.speaker: Frens Ricter
366.text: "That's very disappointing. Even if we're alone in this, the PFJP will keep fighting."

367.speaker: Remus Holstron
367.text: "The correct choice, I would say. The Hawker Court will do the right thing. Nobody should intervene."

368.speaker: Manoly Suheil
368.text: "With all due respect, Mr. Ricter, I think nobody expected a USP president to help with Bludish rights anyway."

369.speaker: Frens Ricter
369.text: "He has. But our position as PFJP is that Article 6 does indeed discriminate against non-Sords."

370.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
370.text: "I truly believe they will be convinced. It is not against their ideology and that is what Colonel Soll intended with the Constitution. We'll be shooting them with their own guns."

371.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
371.text: "Yes. We'll talk about that later, Remus."

380.speaker: Nia Morgna
380.text: "I definitely do not agree with Mr. Kibener or Mr. Holstron. I don't see Sollism's unity working in reality."

381.speaker: Nia Morgna
381.text: "I don't agree with either the Sollist or the neo-Sollist stance of this nation. You already know that."

382.speaker: Nia Morgna
382.text: "But I also have to say that pushing this position could have an effect on the outcome of the case. Mr. Hawker can agree with the traditional Sollist interpretation, after all."

383.speaker: Nia Morgna
383.text: "However, as long as our law enforcement forces are filled with anti-Blud officers, I don't believe the change on the ground will be so visible."

384.speaker: Player
384.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_PFJP"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_NFP_1"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_NFP_2"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_NFP_3"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_NFP_4"] == true) == false)

387.speaker: Nia Morgna
387.text: "I don't like the sound of this."

394.speaker: Petr Vectern
394.text: "I think this is risky, Anton. But if it works -- which it actually might -- it could make a difference."

395.speaker: Petr Vectern
395.text: "If the Court really feels the pressure and accepts it, the lower courts will need to adhere to their interpretation. It might not get rid of legal discrimination, but it could at least decrease it."

396.speaker: Petr Vectern
396.text: "But with the vote on our reforms coming so soon... It's a real leap of faith."

397.speaker: Remus Holstron
397.text: "With all due respect, Mr. Kibener, the NFP cannot merely stay out of it. We must condemn this decision and actively protest it."

398.speaker: Remus Holstron
398.text: "Neither do I. As much as it may be needed, this will only strengthen the Sollism of the USP. We all know Sordists don't agree with Sollist nationalism."

399.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
399.text: "We'll talk about that later, Remus. Sordists will have to listen to me this time."

400.speaker: Manoly Suheil
400.text: "I'll be honest, I didn't expect a USP president to agree to this. You've proved me wrong, Mr. Rayne."

401.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
401.text: "That's a shame, really. Sadly, the NFP cannot take part in this."

402.speaker: Frens Ricter
402.text: "We will also support the effort for the sake of a positive result."

403.speaker: Petr Vectern
403.text: "We appreciate all your comments, ladies and gentlemen, but now that the USP's stance is clear, we should probably end the meeting here."

404.speaker: Frens Ricter
404.text: "And having a positive outcome for this case alone doesn't suffice."

412.speaker: Petr Vectern
412.text: "We shouldn't take this stance while we're trying to amend Article 6 and 7. That inconsistency would damage us."

413.speaker: Petr Vectern
413.text: "Then again, the Supreme Court agrees with it, the lower courts will have to adhere to the interpretation. It might not get rid of legal discrimination, but it could at least decrease it."

416.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
416.conditionsRaw: Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_NFP_1"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_NFP_2"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_NFP_3"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_NFP_4"] == true

417.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
417.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_NFP_1"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_NFP_2"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_NFP_3"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_NFP_4"] == true) == false

419.speaker: Petr Vectern
419.text: "Honestly, it doesn't. As long as there's no big Bludish revolt or anything."

420.speaker: Petr Vectern
420.text: "But regardless, we must do our best to decrease the tensions."

421.speaker: Manoly Suheil
421.text: "What part of it don't you understand? If these legitimate claims are rejected, they will not be raised again in other cases."

422.speaker: Manoly Suheil
422.text: "This will, in practice, only end up legalizing discrimination against all non-Sords."

424.speaker: Frens Ricter
424.text: "That is precisely why our expectation is to see a different result this time. The stakes couldn't be higher."

425.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
425.text: "The only good result would be if the Supreme Court reiterates its commitment to the pillar of 'unity' in Sollism."

426.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
426.text: "If the Court reiterates the definition of 'Sord' in Article 6 as an all-encompassing term, they would be acknowledging that Ersen and others like him are indeed protected by the 'Rights of the Sord Peoples' -- which they are."

427.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
427.text: "As a result, the resettlement policy in Deyr would be reversed, opening the way for Governor Bron's removal and the de-escalation of tensions in Bergia."

428.speaker: Player
428.text: "Why would I want to lose a governor from our party?"
428.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.BergiaSpecialZone_Proposal_Amendment"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.BergiaSpecialZone_Proposal_Centralization"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.BergiaSpecialZone_Proposal_SemiAutonomy"] == true) == false)

429.speaker: Player
429.text: "We are already aware of this case."

431.speaker: Player
431.text: "But what about those who don't want to be called a Sord?"

432.speaker: Player
432.text: "As concerning as this all is, the Supreme Court must make its decision independently. This is not in our jurisdiction, just as lawmaking is not in theirs."

433.speaker: Frens Ricter
433.text: "How about your amendments? Will you leave the Court to decide for themselves there too?"

434.speaker: Player
434.text: "Why do you even care? You and your party are not even giving support to it."

435.speaker: Player
435.text: "Of course not. Their current say in the amendments is wrong, as that shouldn't be the duty of the judiciary. This case, however, is actually their job."

436.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
436.text: "Mr. President... Despite previously being against it, I now completely understand why Sordland still needs Sollism. We need unity more than ever."

437.speaker: Player
437.text: "I trust that they will do the right thing."

438.speaker: Player
438.text: "I am just telling you how it should be, not what will happen."

443.speaker: Petr Vectern
443.text: "Exactly. This looks awfully like a political strategy against the USP."

444.speaker: Nia Morgna
444.text: "I was actively involved in this case. Because of the implications with the constitution, there is no way the Supreme Court will agree with Ishval Ersen on all of the points."

445.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
445.text: "In short, the plan is to release a unified statement to the Justices declaring our support for Ersen and explaining why this is so important."

453.speaker: Player
453.text: "This doesn't fix the core of the problem."

454.speaker: Player
454.text: "That actually makes a lot of sense."

455.speaker: Player
455.text: "Sordland will not be threatened nor blackmailed by some 'massive' response from a group of people."

456.speaker: Remus Holstron
456.text: "If enemies do truly live within our borders, I'd rather they show their true faces earlier than later."

458.speaker: Player
458.text: "Hold on. If this meeting is going to turn into a racist summit, I will take my leave immediately."

459.speaker: Player
459.text: "I will hear you out. But know that I will not act on anything before talking to the representatives of the Bludish community."

461.speaker: Player
461.text: "I am aware of this case. In fact, we are already working on revoking the current special zone status of Bergia."
461.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.BergiaSpecialZone_Proposal_Amendment"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.BergiaSpecialZone_Proposal_Centralization"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.BergiaSpecialZone_Proposal_SemiAutonomy"] == true)

463.speaker: Player
463.text: "I agree completely. In fact, we are already working on the possibility of changing said articles."

465.speaker: Player
465.text: "Doesn't that mean the existence of the Bludish people is literally not being acknowledged?"

467.speaker: Narrator
467.text: Kesaro stared Remus down and continued.

468.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
468.text: "Of course, I'm not saying nothing can change. The results of today's meeting can still, possibly, influence some of our members..."

469.speaker: Narrator
469.text: Nia did not comment but nodded.

470.speaker: Narrator
470.text: Nia smiled for a brief moment and nodded in approval.

475.speaker: Nia Morgna
475.text: "I'll be completely honest. I would never have expected that from you."

476.speaker: Player
476.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_Hub_Option1"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_Hub_Option2"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_Hub_Option3"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_Hub_Option3"] == false)

477.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
477.text: "We have the Minister of Justice here with us too. I'm sure she would not disagree with what I just said."

478.speaker: Frens Ricter
478.text: "You didn't bring this up in our meeting."

480.speaker: Manoly Suheil
480.text: "That's great to hear. We would be very happy if you can share the details once they're more concrete."

481.speaker: Frens Ricter
481.text: "We prefer to push for a precedent for these reforms first. The Ishval Ersen case can give us exactly that."

482.speaker: Frens Ricter
482.text: "Even if you push for amendments, in the case of their failure the current interpretation of the Supreme Court will be the basis of law."

483.speaker: Manoly Suheil
483.text: "We must pressure the Courts to agree with Ersen."

485.speaker: Player
485.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_PFJP_1"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_PFJP_2"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_PFJP_3"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_PFJP_4"] == true) and (Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_NFP_1"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_NFP_2"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_NFP_3"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_NFP_4"] == true)

486.speaker: Frens Ricter
486.text: "We will definitely give support to that when the time comes, Mr. President."

487.speaker: Frens Ricter
487.text: "However, the case of Ishval Ersen has a bigger reach than Bergia."

488.speaker: Frens Ricter
488.text: "That makes things much clearer for us."

492.speaker: Frens Ricter
492.text: "I see that you finally realized that your proposal is doomed. It must be why you're trying to turn your defeat into a symbolic attempt for Bludish rights."

493.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
493.text: "I'll be damned! So the rumors were true after all. Insanity reigns."

494.speaker: Frens Ricter
494.text: "However, we definitely do not see eye to eye with your last-minute hidden details. Adding those to the proposal would destroy its chances."

500.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
500.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_Hub_Option1"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_Hub_Option2"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_Hub_Option3"] == true) == false

503.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
503.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_Hub_Option1"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_Hub_Option2"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_Hub_Option3"] == true) == false

506.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
506.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_Hub_Option1"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_Hub_Option2"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_Hub_Option3"] == true) == false

508.speaker: Petr Vectern
508.text: "I think I have enough information to be able to say we are deep in the mud here."

509.speaker: Narrator
509.text: Petr laughed at his own joke attempt, but nobody else reacted.

511.speaker: Petr Vectern
511.text: "Well... Judging from what Ms. Morgna's been working on, it's safe to say that we have one clear option here. Am I right?"

513.speaker: Petr Vectern
513.text: "Well... I think the NFP's stance could do some good for the Bludish without provoking the establishment. But even that might be risky right before the vote."

517.speaker: Player
517.text: "What do you suggest we do, Ms. Morgna?"
517.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_PFJP_1"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_PFJP_2"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_PFJP_3"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_PFJP_4"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGameIsolated.VictoryDay_ChoiceHub_PFJP_4"] == true) == false)

518.speaker: Narrator
518.text: Petr looked at me and Nia.

519.speaker: Nia Morgna
519.text: "Well, if we are serious about including the amendments to Article 6 and 7 in the current proposal, our stance on this case should be very clear. If there's truly a right time to push for these changes, this is it."

520.speaker: Nia Morgna
520.text: "We should push the Court from all directions. If they reject both the reforms and such a heavily charged court case, everybody will see them for who they are."

521.speaker: Player
521.text: "So you're suggesting we join in with the PFJP's statement?"

522.speaker: Player
522.text: "I disagree. We have to concede one point so as not to agitate them too much. Otherwise both attempts will end up being symbolic only."

523.speaker: Player
523.text: "I agree. We should pressure the Court to admit the discrimination within the Constitution. Let's join in with the PFJP."

524.speaker: Player
524.text: "I'm not convinced. I want to hear from Mr. Ricter and Mr. Kibener first."

525.speaker: Petr Vectern
525.text: "...Unless you want to completely stay out of it?"

567.text: "And according to the Constitution, the language of Sordland is Sordish. If nothing is being done to enforce that, we are breaching the Constitution. This law simply enforces it."

569.speaker: Frens Ricter
569.text: "We have to do something about it. Because the reality is, the secessionists are on the rise..."

570.text: "Just imagine. All parties of the Assembly are reminding them of their duty -- with their own beloved Constitution. Mr. Hawker can't take that pressure."

571.speaker: Kesaro Kibener
571.text: "This is Sordland. You can subscribe to whatever idea you want, but if you are a citizen, you are a Sord. This is how nations work."
